title: Ares: The Iron Vanguard's new update sees you and 15 other players take on a giant flying robot
summary: Ares: The Iron Vanguard offers a mashup of ARPG action and heavy metal fun with its giant power-suits and robotic enemies. Now, in its latest update, Ares: The Iron Vanguard is offering up brand-new cooperative content with the introduction of the Abyss Raid, which will challenge even the most experienced guilds already established! The Abyss Raid is a 15-player (yes, you read that right) cooperative boss battle against Arcarion, an enormous flying robot inspired by deep-sea creatures. You'll need to work together to evade its damaging abilities while destroying cores scattered around the battlefield to take down Arcarion before it takes down you. ... [MORE]

title: Dice of Kalma launches massive new 2.0 update with Dicebound Destiny
summary: Dice of Kalma, the Balatro-like dice roller, is already packed with stuff to do in this battle for your very soul. Now, it's set to get even bigger with the launch of its largest update yet, as Dice of Kalma's 2.0 version lands today, dubbed Dicebound Destiny, and for good reason! And I'm not joking when I call Dicebound Destiny a gamechanger. Because this update introduces a massive new mechanic to Dice of Kalma in the form of reroll abilities. These 11 new abilities, to start, all offer interesting pros and cons for when you reroll, making for an interesting new wrinkle on each build. ... [MORE]

title: UnGodly shows off bloody good barbarian action in its new gameplay trailer
summary: Of all the upcoming releases we've covered, one that's kept my curiosity is UnGodly, the upcoming hack 'n slash RPG from Azra Games and Mark Otero, one of the key figures behind Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes. And in its most recent gameplay trailer, we not only got the announcement that it would be coming to iPhone Duo, but also a good look at its gameplay! It's easy to see why UnGodly is so consistently described as Frazetta-inspired, because everyone lacks a shirt, or at the very least seems to lack the buttons for them. But the action, as simple as it may seem, also benefits from some truly bloody gore effects as your heroes blast apart hapless mooks with everything from simple sword slashes to magic spells. ... [MORE]

title: The Roottrees are Dead has you investigating a complex family tree with 90s technology
summary: Mystery games tend to fall into very familiar divisions, with point-and-click adventures or hidden-object puzzlers as you attempt to unpack a mystery, such as a murder or disappearance. But The Roottrees are Dead offers a very different take on the format as it launches for iOS and Android, complete with an extra mystery! The Roottrees are Dead sees the story kick off with the deaths of the titular wealthy family, and your introduction in the role of investigator. Your job is not to figure out what killed them; that's already clear, but instead you have to track down their various relatives who, thanks to the wishes of an eccentric patriarch, are now entitled to a share of the enormous Roottree fortune. ... [MORE]

title: WB All-Star Mayhem is a new multiverse mashup RPG from Kabam featuring Warner Bros. icons
summary: Nowadays, crossovers are all the rage, be it in movies, comic books or television. And gaming is no different! Now, Kabam are set to tackle the back catalogue of one of entertainment's biggest companies, as WB All-Star Mayhem has been announced for iOS and Android! Set to start limited regional testing this month, WB All-Star Mayhem is a mobile RPG that sees the likes of everything from Adventure Time, Steven Universe, Samurai Jack and Scooby-Doo! cross over, as Animaniac's megalomaniacal mouse Brain gets his hands on a universal remote, with the intention of taking over each universe in turn unless someone puts a stop to him! ... [MORE]

summary: Been on the lookout for an exciting new release to play on mobile? Want to pit fantasy freedom fighters against the forces of an oppressive regime? title: Honkai Nexus Anima set to host its final closed beta offering you a glimpse at more new stuff
summary: Of all the upcoming releases we've had our eyes on, one of the most interesting has been that of Honkai: Nexus Anima. MiHoYo's stab at a creature collector, mixed with their typical flashy ARPG action, has been slowly chugging along towards release for many months. Now, its final closed beta is set to go live on November 25th. Honkai: Nexus Anima itself is set to launch in Spring of 2027, but the final beta takes us back to the city of Lia, introducing even more mechanics that'll be present in the final product. Many of these are simply building on the existing foundation, with new characters, Anima, and adventures to be had. ... [MORE]

title: Once Human sees you lay down the sound in season five, Dissonant Resonance, coming soon
summary: Once Human and its bizarre, paranormal world has played host to some strange seasons over its lifespan, most recently taking you into battle on the high seas against an enormous crab. Now, things are getting even stranger as Once Human's fifth season has been unveiled, titled Dissonant Resonance, set to land on November 19th. If the title didn't clue you in, season five of Once Human is focused on music and sound. A brand-new, ominous, looming creature, a pipe-organ leviathan, will watch the battlefield, changing conditions in response to your actions. You'll even face down the colossus itself in a new four-player raid, where it's a race against time to finish it off before the music track concludes, with dynamic changes tied to the song. ... [MORE]

title: Crossy Road Rush sees the hit Frogger-like go full endless runner, out now on Apple Arcade
summary: Of all the games that take a concept that's already been done and turn it into a success, I think Crossy Road qualifies as one of the more successful. Hot off the back of Flappy Bird's success, Crossy Road Rush revamped the formula and combined it with Frogger to great effect. Now, however, developer Hipster Whale have gone in a whole new direction with Crossy Road Rush! Available now on Apple Arcade, Crossy Road Rush turns the familiar Frogger-style runner into something more like Subway Surfers in terms of format. Rather than hopping over lanes and obstacles, you'll be rushing down the road yourself, dodging from side to side as your favourite Crossy Road characters. ... [MORE]

title: Call of Duty Mobile reveals full details and launch date for Verdansk, dropping in soon
summary: Call of Duty Mobile has been a perennial favourite of shooter fans on mobile, even outliving the much-hyped Call of Duty Warzone: Mobile. Now, as if to cement that dominance, Call of Duty Mobile will see the addition of the iconic Verdansk map, which kicked off the popularity of the original Warzone! As teased all the way back at the start of October, Verdansk is set to land soon, on November 11th, in fact. And it comes packed with 15 different points of interest, such as the Stadium and Airport, that will be familiar to any fan of Call of Duty Warzone, while the iconic Gulag also makes a return to allow you one shot at returning to the field once you die. ... [MORE]

title: A Fool's Errand is a one-dimensional climber where your ascent is measured in swipes
summary: It seems rather fitting that just earlier I was writing up my review for Titanium Court (see it soon!) and this crossed my desk. Once an inhabitant of the Playdate platform, A Fool's Errand has unexpectedly become available for purchase on iOS. But, what exactly makes this game such a natural fit for mobile? Well, as you might expect A Fool's Errand was originally set to make use of the Playdate's signature crank, which would manage how fast your humble hero Roland ascended the sinister staircase. You used the crank to ascend, dodging traps and enemies as you went. So with only a single means of control it certainly isn't losing anything by jumping to mobile. ... [MORE]

title: Gunboat God sets November launch date for its crocodile-powered shoot 'em up
summary: Your mechanic in Gunboat God is a crocodile called Yeti. I’ve read that back a few times now and it still doesn’t make any more sense, but he’s apparently the best in the trade and a genuinely good guy, so I’ll stop asking questions. He’s heading to iOS and Android with the rest of this side-scrolling shoot ’em up, and to Switch as well. You’re stuck somewhere you don’t recognise, trying to get back to a Citadel in the sky, and the best thing you’ve got is a boat with an alarming amount of firepower bolted to it. Getting home means going through more than twenty mission types. Collision Course and Outlast explain themselves, while one is just called Boil. ... [MORE]

title: Old School RuneScape lets you test your mettle with the introduction of Hardcore Worlds
summary: Old School RuneScape and the whole RuneScape-verse has been going for nigh-on 20 years now, and for those looking for a challenge, there are plenty of bosses and dungeons to face. But now, even the most experienced of players can face a true trial, as today, Hardcore Worlds arrive in Old School RuneScape on all platforms, mobile included. Hardcore Worlds function exactly as you'd expect them to, but if you're new to the concept, here's a brief explainer: In Hardcore Worlds, death is final. As in no retries, no restarts. Whether it's slow or sudden, if your character perishes, you can either discard them or transfer them to a regular server, though without the rewards or goodies available exclusively on Hardcore Worlds. ... [MORE]

title: Monsta brings a turn-based portable classic to mobile, where it's you versus mutant monsters
summary: For many of us, the history of mobile gaming only stretches back to the first iPhone, and maybe a little further if we head back to the days of flip phones and the N-Gage. But look even further back, to when PDAs (Personal Digital Assistants) were all the craze, and you'll find examples of the primordial soup of mobile gaming, such as Monsta. First released back in the 2000s on PalmOS devices, and now available for the modern-day iOS and Android platforms, Monsta had to tackle many hardware limitations, including slow processing speed at the time. That's what inspired developer Superverse Industries to create this turn-based tactical shooter, where it's just you and a building full of monsters to get before they get you. ... [MORE]

title: Elder Scrolls: Sentinel has been named though not dated, but Elder Scrolls: Castles is here for a mobile fix
summary: Hallelujah! It seems that Bethesda Softworks have finally kicked themselves into gear, with the announcement that the hotly anticipated Elder Scrolls VI will be called Sentinel. And... Oh, turns out, that's all. Guess we're back to waiting, but if you need something to tide you over, did you know you can play The Elder Scrolls on mobile? Well, one of its spinoffs at the very least. With the shuttering of The Elder Scrolls: Blades earlier this year, options can seem thin on the ground. But dig a little deeper, and you'll find that Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls: Castles, which lets you build and manage your own fortress and family dynasty, offers you a hefty taste of Tamriel on the go!  ... [MORE]

title: Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra delays long-awaited major overhaul
summary: Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra, the 4v4 brawler that sees you and your friends pitted against other players as characters from Akira Toriyama's iconic manga, has delayed its hotly anticipated overhaul update. While originally scheduled for the end of the year, the patch has now been pushed back to March of 2027. Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra's overhaul patch was set to make major changes, including a third-person camera perspective, simplified rulesets, and changes to both customisation and roles. While normal patches will keep rolling out, you'll have to wait a bit longer for the full overhaul to land. ... [MORE]

summary: Ever since Godzilla was stomping around Tokyo like a big playground, one question has been on everyone's mind: Let them fight. Big monsters are cool, so big monster versus big monster is even cooler, and that simple equation is exactly what Passion Republic Games' GigaBash Mobile is the solution to! title: The Farmer Was Replaced brings its million-selling coding simulator to iOS and Android
summary: Consider this: a million copies sold of a game where you write code to run a farm. I wouldn’t have bet on that, but The Farmer Was Replaced got there, and it’s out now on iOS and Android with its new DLC, The Miner Was Replaced, thrown in. You write short programs in a Python-like language, hit execute, and a drone does the tilling, planting and harvesting based on whatever you wrote. No levels, just a steady run of unlocks and problems, like merging pumpkins into one giant one or hunting for treasure in a hedge maze. And if you already code, you can skip the basics and go straight to running a fleet of drones. ... [MORE]
